research_progress.source_confidence_semantics: Heuristic research-source confidence only: official GOV.UK, Environment Agency and Planning Data sources directly verified on the web on 24 July 2026; currentness/provenance, legal-process separation, NO_DATA handling and exact-parcel fail-closed controls. Not parcel-level accuracy.

official_sources.name: Open space, sports and recreation facilities, public rights of way and local green space
official_sources.fact: Government planning guidance says open space should be considered in plan-making and development decisions and explains Local Green Space designation.
official_sources.gate: Open-space or Local Green Space policy relevance is not by itself an exact parcel boundary, planning refusal or development permission.

official_sources.name: NPPF chapter 8: promoting healthy and safe communities
official_sources.fact: Current NPPF policy requires robust, up-to-date open-space evidence and restricts loss of existing open space unless specified surplus, replacement or alternative-sport tests are satisfied.
official_sources.gate: Open-space policy tests require proposal-specific evidence; designation or proximity alone does not determine a parcel outcome.

official_sources.name: Planning Data local green space dataset
official_sources.fact: Planning Data reports 0 Local Green Space records, 0 providers and no collection attempt, with MHCLG-created placeholder provenance.
official_sources.gate: Zero platform rows means NO_DATA, not proof that an exact parcel is outside a locally designated Local Green Space.

official_sources.name: Minerals planning guidance
official_sources.fact: Government minerals guidance explains Mineral Safeguarding Areas and Mineral Consultation Areas and the need to avoid needless sterilisation of important mineral resources.
official_sources.gate: A safeguarded mineral resource does not create a presumption that it will be worked, and mapped safeguarding is not planning permission or refusal.

official_sources.name: NPPF chapter 17: facilitating the sustainable use of minerals
official_sources.fact: Current NPPF policy requires mineral safeguarding, prior extraction where practical and safeguarding of minerals handling and transport infrastructure.
official_sources.gate: Minerals safeguarding is a policy constraint and consultation trigger, not proof of extractability, viability or final planning outcome.

official_sources.name: Planning Data mineral safeguarding area dataset
official_sources.fact: Planning Data currently reports 0 Mineral Safeguarding Area records, 0 providers and no collection attempt.
official_sources.gate: Zero platform rows means NO_DATA and must not be interpreted as absence of a local Mineral Safeguarding Area or Mineral Consultation Area.

official_sources.name: National planning policy for waste
official_sources.fact: National waste planning policy requires waste infrastructure and development to be considered alongside housing, transport, health and environmental protection.
official_sources.gate: Waste-policy compatibility is not an environmental permit, planning permission or proof that waste infrastructure is available to a target site.

official_sources.name: Waste: environmental permits
official_sources.fact: Environment Agency guidance updated 12 February 2026 distinguishes exemptions, standard-rules permits and bespoke permits for waste activities.
official_sources.gate: Planning permission, waste-policy allocation or a permit category does not prove a permit has been granted for a specific operator or site.

official_sources.name: Apply for an environmental permit
official_sources.fact: Environment Agency guidance published 12 February 2026 and updated 26 February 2026 explains application routes for activities that can cause pollution, increase flood risk or affect land drainage.
official_sources.gate: Submitting or being eligible to submit a permit application is not evidence of permit grant, planning permission or operational readiness.

official_sources.name: Check if you need an environmental permit
official_sources.fact: Guidance updated 2 March 2026 explains when environmental permits or licences may be needed for activities that could pollute or affect flood risk, drainage or water resources.
official_sources.gate: A screening conclusion about whether a permit may be needed does not prove a site can lawfully operate or that all other consents are satisfied.

official_sources.name: Get advice before you apply for an environmental permit
official_sources.fact: Environment Agency pre-application guidance updated 1 May 2026 provides basic and enhanced advice before an environmental permit application.
official_sources.gate: Pre-application advice is not a permit, planning permission or binding final regulatory decision.

official_sources.name: Legal operator and competence requirements: environmental permits
official_sources.fact: Guidance updated 11 June 2026 sets legal, financial and professional competence requirements for environmental permit operators, with additional waste-operator duties.
official_sources.gate: A technically competent operator does not prove a specific permit is granted, active or spatially relevant to a target parcel.

official_sources.name: Environmental permit application forms: standard rules, installations, mining waste or waste operation
official_sources.fact: The Environment Agency permit-form collection links current 2026 waste guidance and application forms, including forms updated in May 2026.
official_sources.gate: Availability or completion of a form is administrative readiness only and is not permit grant or planning consent.

official_sources.name: Control and monitor emissions for your environmental permit
official_sources.fact: Environment Agency guidance sets expectations for controlling and monitoring point-source and other emissions under environmental permits.
official_sources.gate: Permit monitoring requirements do not establish that a proposed site has a permit, acceptable emissions or planning approval.

official_sources.name: Developers: get environmental advice on your planning proposals
official_sources.fact: Guidance updated 1 July 2026 explains when developers can seek Natural England, Environment Agency and other environmental advice and keeps planning and environmental consents distinct.
official_sources.gate: Agency advice or paid pre-application engagement is not planning permission, an environmental permit or site-specific approval.

official_sources.name: Land stability planning guidance
official_sources.fact: Government planning guidance explains that landslides, subsidence and ground heave may require land- or slope-stability risk assessment and mitigation.
official_sources.gate: A regional or mapped instability indication is not a measured geotechnical condition or proof that development is unsafe or suitable.

official_sources.name: Light pollution planning guidance
official_sources.fact: Planning guidance says artificial lighting should be considered for developments that add lighting or are sensitive to existing lighting, including effects on people, wildlife and dark landscapes.
official_sources.gate: Dark-sky context or nearby lighting is not a parcel-specific lighting impact result; scheme design, timing and intensity must be assessed.

official_sources.name: Land affected by contamination planning guidance
official_sources.fact: Planning guidance requires development land to be suitable for its new use and distinguishes planning from Part 2A, Building Regulations and environmental permitting controls.
official_sources.gate: Historic land use or a contamination flag is not proof of unacceptable risk, remediation completion or planning refusal.

official_sources.name: Land contamination technical guidance collection
official_sources.fact: Environment Agency technical guidance updated 13 May 2026 groups risk-based controls for contaminated land, groundwater, human health, ecological receptors and ground gases.
official_sources.gate: Technical guidance is an assessment framework, not a site investigation result, Part 2A determination or remediation sign-off.

official_sources.name: Voluntary remediation advice for contaminated land and groundwater
official_sources.fact: Environment Agency guidance published 3 June 2026 offers site-specific advisory review where contamination has affected controlled waters and makes the developer or landowner responsible for site safety.
official_sources.gate: Voluntary remediation advice is advisory and is not planning permission, a statutory remediation determination or environmental permit.

official_sources.name: Contaminated land and groundwater: generic developed principles
official_sources.fact: Environment Agency principles updated 30 March 2026 address contaminated land and groundwater pathways in the context of radioactive material and Part 2A regulation.
official_sources.gate: These principles have a specific regulatory scope and must not be generalized into a parcel contamination conclusion without applicable evidence.

official_sources.name: Deposit for recovery operators: environmental permits
official_sources.fact: Environment Agency guidance updated 20 May 2026 explains waste-recovery-plan and permit requirements for deposit-for-recovery operations.
official_sources.gate: A recovery plan or standard-rule route does not prove the activity qualifies as recovery, the permit is granted or planning permission exists.

official_sources.name: Planning Data brownfield land dataset
official_sources.fact: Planning Data reports 37,666 brownfield land records from 354 providers, with collector run 23 July 2026 and all data described as authoritative.
official_sources.gate: Brownfield-register inclusion signals development potential but does not prove planning permission, land control, delivery or exact canonical parcel relation.

official_sources.name: Planning Data brownfield site experimental dataset
official_sources.fact: Planning Data reports 2,916 experimental brownfield-site boundaries from five providers and states the dataset is MHCLG-created pending authoritative replacement.
official_sources.gate: Experimental brownfield geometry must not be treated as authoritative parcel geometry or current permission status.

official_sources.name: Planning Data asset of community value dataset
official_sources.fact: Planning Data reports 101 Assets of Community Value; it states ACV listing does not itself restrict what an owner can do, though it may be a material consideration and a Local Land Charge.
official_sources.gate: ACV status is not a blanket development prohibition, planning refusal or proof of community ownership.

official_sources.name: Planning Data built up area dataset
official_sources.fact: Planning Data reports 7,157 built-up areas from ONS for statistical purposes, with collector run 23 July 2026.
official_sources.gate: A statistical built-up-area boundary is not a planning allocation, settlement boundary, permission or exact parcel development status.

official_sources.name: Planning Data central activities zone dataset
official_sources.fact: Planning Data reports 10 Central Activities Zone geographies from three providers, collector run 23 July 2026, with some MHCLG-created data pending authoritative replacement.
official_sources.gate: CAZ membership is policy context and mixed-provenance geography; it does not itself determine planning permission or parcel suitability.

official_sources.name: How to assess and allocate sites for development
official_sources.fact: MHCLG guidance published 31 March 2026 covers site assessment, drafting site-allocation policy and site-assessment templates.
official_sources.gate: Site assessment or draft allocation work is plan-making evidence, not adopted allocation, planning permission or delivery certainty.
